[LTAC.3.6] If the `after` body references no LHS bindings, the
compiler must skip the capture-fact emission. Empty captures are
not emitted.

This differs from a correlated call, which emits the capture fact even with
nothing to capture ([LCCO.5.2], [LCCO.5.6]). There the capture fact is what
carries a generated or computed correlation to the sibling rules. Here the
timer fact carries the correlation itself ([LTAC.3.5]), so an empty capture
fact would carry nothing the follow-up rule needs.

idris.name: ltac_3_5__captured
idris.note: A body reading nothing is captured by the empty list: no capture is minted. VACUOUS for this clause: the model mints no capture fact for any body, the captures riding on the timer's payload, so 'the compiler must skip the capture-fact emission' holds of it with nothing to skip. A fixture.

idris.name: ltac_3_6__no_capture
idris.note: THE EMPTY CAPTURE: a body that reads nothing; the timer's key and payload both the empty tuple's code. 'Empty captures are not emitted': nothing rides on the timer. VACUOUS for this clause: the model has no capture fact at all, so none is emitted whether or not the body reads a binding. A fixture.
